english: How lovely of you to join us, Cleric.
The orc nods towards the shining beacon of a guest floating in front of the fireplace.
You should speak with him.
E-...Okay.
You approach the orc as she's working through some papers on the sofa.
She barely looks up at you.
I turned in some more AEFAs.
Hey.
(Just stare at her and breathe heavily.)
Viira jolts as she notices you.
Oh! Hello, Cleric. I didn't even notice you come in...
She gets up and places the documents in a drawer.
(Walk over to her.)
Among fancy furniture, and before the crackling fireplace, you see an orc. She raises her head towards you when you approach.
Ah. You must be the Urthguard gentleman I've heard so much about.
She hides it well, but the orc is stressed. Perhaps it has to do with the dwarves.
Exuding an air of authority around her, the large woman gives you a wry smile. Her tusks are gleaming.
Welcome to the Askanii-Reeds Trading Company.
Not just physically imposing, this orc knows how to exert power in other ways as well.
You spot the merchant's mark on her jacket sleeve - a heart with the initials of the Norvikian Freestrider regiment.
You sure walk around like a damn advertisement with this drab uniform.
As he SHOULD.
She presents her palm to you. "Viira is my name. I am Second-in-Command Guild Agent of Tolstad."
Nice to meet you...
Yes, the handsome orc lady wants you to say a name.
Be nice to her! She's a Freestrider.
Make sure she knows you are a CLERIC.
The showing of the palm is a casual cultural greeting in Reeds.
Do not grab her hand. That's not what that is.
Take her hand. She would love that.
(Grab her hand.)
I'm Ragn.
I'm a Rogue.
I'm The Cleric, actually.
Names and labels aren't important.
You reach forward and take her hand in yours. She's clearly a bit confused.
She did not expect this.
It becomes a sort of awkward handshake.
You realize her hand is a fair bit larger than yours. She could easily match your tremendous force.
You realize her hand is a fair bit larger than yours, and something stings in your soul. Fragile as it is, a part of you has been bruised by the simple thought of her overwhelming power.
Yes... now kiss it.
(Let go of her hand.)
(Kiss her hand.)
She gives you a polite smile.
You lean in and attempt to bonk the front of your helmet against the top of her hand.
She quickly pulls it back. With a laugh she says, "Perhaps a name is in order first, human."
She appears mildly entertained by your strange behavior. Maybe she would enjoy more of it?
Hello, Ragn.
Rogue? Like a... swashbuckler? Intriguing.
She should be. It's really cool.
The Cleric? Ah.
She loves it. Your stoic presence is enough to induce intrigue and awe.
Apologies. Not Urthguard. Cleric. I assumed the terms were interchangeable.
But I suppose you're not all... she says, waving towards your outfit. "Esoterically attuned."
Not all Urthguard are spellcasters. Not all clerics are Urthguard. But all clerics are spellcasters.
She accepts your annoying correction with a smile.
Probably means she sees you as no threat at all. A mere puppy.
Debatable. But I do like a secretive man.
She shoots you another smile, waiting patiently for you to say anything.
The orc stands among fancy furniture. A crackling fireplace lights up her face as you approach.
Hot.
Welcome to the Askanii-Reeds Trading Company, Cleric.
It is the orc lady again. Beware her manipulation.
Yes, and also... tell her she looks lovely.
Big... orc.
No...! Nooo!
Hello, Agent. How's the Freestriding going?
Right. You're the orc who was fighting with the dwarves.
You... big... orc.
You look lovely to meet you again, Agent Viira.
That's... not a verb I usually hear.
But it's going well!
We're currently deep in paperwork with a new partner.
A lot of work.
She lets out a hearty laugh. "Fighting, you say?"
In all honesty, I wouldn't mind a real scrap at this point.
Her eyebrows shoot into the fucking ceiling.
Oh. Are you okay, Cleric?
(Admire her.)
She stares at you for a few seconds as you stare back.
Anyway.
Hm? Oh.
She blinks thrice and then just nods, ignoring your flub.
Yes. Of course. Same to you.
Damn it...!
Not very smooth, dick-ass.
She walks over to the desk, grabbing a piece of paper.
It could be a good idea to search the Guild Warehouse, below.
Not only to find some goodies... but also to check what's going in and out the city.
The Warehouse, below here...
It probably holds a lot of useful stuff.
This wonderful Freestrider lady is the one who decides who comes and goes. So... talk her into letting you enter her warehouse.
If you ask that, she will think you mean something very different.
I admit, it's not often I'm led by the nose like that.
But I suppose clerics are in their right to cast Charm Person on anyone they please in this city.
Although I heard the dwarves did not hold their rally after all. So I suppose they retain some sense in those thick skulls of theirs.
I apologize about that. It seemed like a good idea at the time.
You were out of control. I had to do it.
What's done is done. Now can we get to business?
Hm. Well. Apology accepted.
Her eyes say otherwise.
Huh. That was easy!
Pff...!
She stops herself from laughing.
It would have been a mocking laugh.
Fair enough.
She is holding back rage. Deep rage.
You act in interesting ways, Cleric.
Now, I'm very busy. We're currently deep in paperwork with a new partner.
It seems you were correct in the end. Your diplomatic efforts ended with the dwarves not holding their little rally.
So, well done.
Not the win you were hoping for, I suppose. But I did solve the problem.
You should have listened to me earlier.
Oh, don't worry. I'm not petty.
Huh. Could've sworn she was.
Hm.
Confident, are we?
She's annoyed at your arrogance. But also kind of likes it.
Of course, I'm very busy. We're currently deep in paperwork with a new partner.
I'll never forget that punch, Cleric.
Probably not the most difficult challenge to goad a dwarf like Alfoz, but taking it like that?
Highly impressive.
Thanks. It hurt.
I didn't do it for you.
I... did it for you.
Understandable!
I sure hope not!
That's... nice of you.
She cringes. Oh, so badly.
Now, things are a bit busy here.
But I can always make time for a friend of the Freestrider cause.
Well done, handling the dwarves.
Made my life a lot easier, at the very least.
Anytime.
Good! There might certainly be more things we could use a cleric's help with...
But I can always make time to a friend of the Freestrider cause.
I can gladly report to you that the business with the dwarves was eventually solved after you left.
Through entirely peaceful methods, thankfully.
Oh really?
How?
Good job.
I don't care.
Thank you, Cleric.
She lets out some air from her nose.
She is a bit annoyed at your brash nature, but also finds it refreshing.
Good. Then let us move on.
A contact at the palace helped me recruit two Vourgeni gentlemen.
The giant kind of gentlemen. When Alfoz saw them coming, he very quickly packed everything up and left.
To tell the truth, I hoped for them to put up some resistance.
Sorry for not staying and helping clean things up.
You used the threat of violence to push past their legal arguments, then?
You had no reason to interfere. No worries.
She gives you a smug smirk.
Yes.
A powerful statement.
She knows when to bend and when to break, clearly.
Nice.
Sounds fascist.
That is your choice. I have no opinion on your choice. Mainly because I am apolitical.
She chuckles.
That's a big word!
Proud of you, she says and winks.
Oh. Right.
Sounds like you would be a very useful collaborator in that case.
Thank you... Cleric.
Yes. Thanks.
(Start slow clapping.)
...Thank you.
Thank you.
Now, is there anything the Askanii-Reeds Trade Co. can help you with today, Cleric?
Cleric. What can the AR do for you?
Cleric. I'm working late today, as you can see.
She is very much trying to not look directly at your head. Due to the bucket.
She is very much trying to not look directly at your head. Due to the pot.
The orc glares at you.
Can I-
Maybe it's-
I should go.
Nothing I see. Well, good day.
You're not getting back from this.
She will not speak to you, because of what you did.
You idiot. Oh well.
(Leave.)
She gives you a short smile.
Treachery.
She gives you her trademark smile.
Though I do that almost every day, if you can believe it.
She is clearly, clearly, terribly angry at you, still.
Don't make this any worse, will you? Snell whispers to you.
She's not still mad at you... is she?
I have some questions...
I want to search the warehouse.
Persuade her to work with you, despite your previous behavior.
E-"That's all for now. Thank you, citizen."
Oh, I'm afraid I don't have time right now, Cleric.
Perhaps you could book a meeting? I'd love to help, of course.
When are you available?
Some other time, then.
Ah, em...
How about March 29th?
That's too late.
But... that's all the way after the election!
I'll take it.
I am sorry, but I'm really just swamped here!
I am sorry, but I'm really just swamped here.
Great! See you then!
Mm.
She has no intention of having a meeting with you.
You're gonna have to turn on the charm, if you ever want to get anything out of her now.
You sense a threatening aura.
This is what happens when you make an enemy of a Freestrider.
Guess you'll just have to wait until... after the election.
But that's like, very far in the future!
Several days!
Oh, do you?
We can arrange that. After the election, of course. Like I said, things are just very busy right now.
Another excuse. She's good at this!
You're not actually busy, are you? You're just mad at me.
Okay.
She drops her smile.
Mad? I suppose I disagree with your methods, Cleric. But I promise you.
I am a professional. I do not let petty things like that get in the way.
Good. Let's talk later.
Okay. It's time to solve this.
Smooth-talking-style.
So like, manipulation?
Something like that.
Just give her a little something. Then she'll give in.
Viira.
Mm? Yes?
And make it clear that it's a good deal. For both parties.
The Askanii-Reeds Trading Company can stand to gain a lot from my help.
Can it?
Yes. As can I from yours. (Lean in.)
Well from what I saw up there, I-
The deal with the dwarves worked out in my favor, for a number of reasons. But that was a different deal. Right now, we can both stand to gain.
She glares at you. Looking you up and down.
Then her gaze softens. She sighs.
Perhaps there is time.
I assist you, you assist me. Isn't that right?
Deal.
So what do you want, Cleric?
Her voice is rather cold still, but she clearly enjoys your business-first attitude.
Threat avoided.
You stare at her, as she keeps avoiding your gaze.
There is... no way you're doing this right now.
Just stay quiet. She's so much more powerful than you ever will be.
Although maybe... if you beg, it might actually help your chances.
V-Viira. Please talk to me.
(Stay quiet.)
She glances at you with a frown.
I am, Cleric. But I am, like I've mentioned, quite busy.
Please... (Grovel.)
Cleric. Cleric. No.
PLEASE.
Cleric! I...
She sighs.
Maybe later. I'm busy now. Okay?
Okay. Good.
She finds you disgusting.
As she should...
How dishonorable.
She smooths out her jacket.
You done?
Tell me more about the Freestriders.
What's with the thing in the fireplace?
I want to know more about you.
I'm not a THING!
Don't mind him. He's harmless.
I don't know exactly how we came over the contract, but I believe it was a Kargameshian fellow who handed it over.
A smoke mephit. It keeps track of unwanted visitors.
So don't touch anything, Cleric. Unless you like getting seared.
She smiles. Her tusks gleam.
My favorite topic!
That's good. Good. Neat.
You're your... your own favorite...
Neat?
Neat.
Neat.
Hm?
You're your own... you are your own favorite topic?
Yes!
She might, possibly, be acting cheeky.
She's one confusing orc.
About her past. So you can manipulate her.
Don't do that.
Yeah. Go ahead.
Sorry?
Master talk about Meek? Ahoy-hoy!
Her jaw drops.
Then her fists go up.
No, no. He's not strangling me or anything. He's just helping me.
(Raise your fists too.) "I would die to protect this smile."
Meek serve master!
Master is great!
She shakes her head as if dazed by the visuals.
I see.
I have not heard of a tame mimic before.
She lowers her fists. Slowly.
He's not tame, per se...
He's very tame. Docile, even.
(Shrug.) "I found him below. It is what it is."
Then you are even braver than I thought.
Meek is nice!
Tell that to the Pest Control Guild.
Well, Cleric. You're full of surprises.
But please keep that thing... uhm... hidden around here.
Just in case we get any guests.
Griffon on the Roof!
The orc laughs at your words.
That really sounds like a magazine tale. I swear I've read it at some point.
...What?
I am serious. There is a griffon upstairs.
It really does!
Oh, nevermind.
Yes, yes- I thought it sounded funny is all.
Right?
Technically, the griffon is not allowed to use our building as a nest. However, by sheer happenstance, it has become one of the many unwritten and unofficial exceptions around here.
I have simply learned to make do. As one does.
Who owns it?
And it just sleeps here all day?
Is it annoying to deal with?
Can I fly on it?
M-"That's all about the griffon."
One of our temporary guests.
A high-ranking member of the Freestriders, come to visit for the election. One of those types.
...Our dear Prince Moonwatch, in fact.
For now. I've heard he'll be heading out after the election. Can't wait.
Though the real answer to that involved describing griffon-droppings, and I'd prefer to keep away from that.
I'd recommend not, entirely for the sake of your own health.
Unless you've got somewhere to fly off to?
I do not, no.
Damn it. I don't. If I did, I'd totally try it.
Your health is happy to hear it.
Somehow, I could imagine.
Yes. Let's leave it at that.
Viira is not happy about the situation.
Viira is avoiding answering many things about this creature.
For one: because she does not wish to think about it. For second: because she is not allowed to say anything about its owner.
Bureaucratic reason, sure.
Meriadoc flies on that beast, then.
You would LOVE to have a griffon one day.
You could be like the heroes of your childhood tales.
Soaring through the air...
RIDER OF THE SKY.
Dream on, baby. Dream on.
And where was he?
You're not shocked?
Down below.
No.
Where?
Below?
All the way down on Underhollow Ridge. He was captured by a troll.
She groans, walking over to the desk.
Of course he was.
He's in one piece I take it?
More or less.
He was smiling when I got him out of that cage.
No. For he is not a fictional character.
Great.
...Of course he was.
Not the time for obscure references, Cleric.

You see, our dear Moonwatch Prince came to visit us a few days ago. He journeyed for the election yes, but from what I understand it was also to seek out the ruins below the city. For his... research.
No wonder he ended up in trouble.
Viira sighs before tossing you a pouch. "Here. For your service to the revolution!"
Oh! (Grab the pouch.)
Let's keep this on the down-low, shall we?
She opens her mouth and thinks for a moment before clarifying, "That means: do not talk about how one of our most prestigious celebrities almost got eaten by a troll- okay?"
Got it.
I can't promise anything.
Do I have a choice?
Good.
Those coins in your hand seem to prove otherwise.
A grin and a waltz towards you later, and the orc leans in near your helmed face. "Now tell me..."
Did you actually fight the troll?
Then to Snell: "Did you?"
The goblin lets out a sigh.
Oh yeah. I killed the troll.
We fought. It was a hard-earned victory.
It was almost a slaughter- but I got lucky in the end.
My goodness. A real trollkiller in our midst...
He does deserve that credit.
I was backup.
That's very impressive nonetheless!
Oh my. The Coinlord's bodyguard?
You managed to bring her all the way down there?
Yes. I was simply too charming for her to resist.
She was nice enough to join us.
She was eager to fight.
Say it ain't so- I'm getting jealous here, Cleric!
That's not the Ettir I've met- I'm sure you had some effect on her, Cleric...
Oh, I bet. It must have been spectacular!
Oh, so humble...
A quick laugh, and then she returns to her desk to look over a document.
I'll have to speak with Moonwatch about it later. Whenever he chooses to grace us with his presence once again.
Once more I must say: I am very grateful to have you here, Cleric. Thank you.
Now, is there anything else the AR can do for you on this fine day- just let me know.
Oh, that?
Just a little something left behind by my superior during his latest visit.
Don't touch it, please.
You can have it, if you want.
Really?
Thank you, my lady.
So your boss won't miss it?
Sure. Why not?
She gives you a smile.
A false smile.
My boss isn't here. I'm in charge.
Go ahead, Cleric.
She's happy to take control.
Hm. Yeah, something about her 'superior' is clearly a weak spot.
She happily gives you the scroll.
Primarily as revenge against this superior, yes.
Oh!
Well...
I... she mutters, looking completely stumped.
She carefully glances towards the hidden safe's location.
I am quite honestly stumped, Cleric.
I was not even aware we'd been robbed.
But quite sincerely, thank you!
This is... more than I can even repay you.
Just help me out in the future, and we'll be square.
I just wanted to help my Freestrider friends.
Don't mention it.
She spreads her arms and in an act of relief, and still a bit of shock, she gives you a big hug.
Heh.
Ladies' man here.
Alas, are the days of LOL... over?
I promise you, Cleric.
You will be paid back for this. I swear. Come back here after the election, and I'll have something GREAT for you. I guarantee it!
It's a promise!
A cleric searching for a hag...
That really sounds like a magazine tale. Romantic, almost.
No. It sounds like an epic quest.
Yes. Very romantic.
Have you seen a hag around here?
She laughs.
Oh, I'm inclined to agree.
Highly so.

Look. It's no secret the Askanii-Reeds Trade Co. employs a number of hags. Since the early revolution, we've prided ourselves in working with those who turned from the magocrats. Including the many young women left scarred after the MHR.
MHR?
...So you're employing hags on Tolstad?
Mass Hag Recruitment.
A terrible initiative in Old Diminor.
A freelancer. Yes.
Her name is Lisa. She provides security, arcane knowledge, eldritch invocations, and divination.
She's quite good.
But unfortunately she is off on a private matter, from what I understand. So she is unavailable at the moment.
When did she leave?
Is she involved with the tea shop?
Where does she live?
Can she cast fireballs?
So she's a witch?
Where can I find her?
Okay. Let me know if she shows up.
I'm not entirely sure.
Last week? Something like that?
Did she leave right around the time of the tea shop explosion?
Be specific.
You don't keep track of your workers?
It's possible.
She shrugs. "I apologize. I can't say for sure."
Our freelancers are kept on a very light and long leash.
Not from what I know.
Although I do understand if it's something you'd keep an eye on.
I imagine any esoterically minded individual or creature in the city would be under suspicion.
Even our hard-working hag.
In a hut. It's usually parked on top of our headquarters here.
Parked?
It moves. You know how hags are.
Oh, I don't think so.
I remember those funny magma hags on the Burned Coast, but beyond that I don't think I've ever heard of a hag casting spells like that.
Lisa only deals with typical hag magic.
She thinks about your questions for a while.
I think there's a distinct difference between hags and witches, but I'm not entirely sure what they are.
This orc is the wrong person to ask about esoteric things, I'm afraid!
No clue! Freelancers go where they please.
She might have left the city as far as I know. She'll turn up eventually though, I'm sure.
Will do, Cleric.
She drops her empty expression, giving you a relieved sigh.
She's a good one.
Where was she hiding?
The City Below.
It's a secret.
Really? Well, if anyone can make it down there, it's our Lisa.
She nods. "Yes, better if it stays between you two."
Good job on locating her. It must have been hard.
I hope you found what you were looking for?
I did. And I've got questions for you.
I know about the meeting in the tea shop.
You're in big trouble, Agent Viira.
Don't worry. I'll answer.
I figured.
She smiles. "No. I don't think so."
We sent Lisa to deal with a potential customer of the AR.
But luckily she was not caught in the blast. She wasn't even there.
Did you know about this meeting?
They were meeting to trade an artifact. Do you know what kind?
That's all about Lisa. For now.
